data.body: Phase 1 RCA (rebar-debug): CI run 33426859481 Windows job fails twice with `ValueError: the environment variable is longer than 32767 characters` in pytest itself while setting `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` (`_pytest.runner._update_current_test_var`, log lines 26379-26390 and 26441-26453). The offending node is `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_comment_marker_survives_truncation.py::test_undecorated_text_is_byte_identical_to_the_bare_fitter[far_over_limit-<60000 x chars>]`: the parameter tuple includes the actual 60,000-character string, so pytest’s default param id embeds it in the nodeid and then in `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST`. Local discriminating experiment on macOS constructed that same value and a Windows-cap shim raised the same `ValueError` at length 60171, proving the mechanism without Windows. Legitimacy: defect in the test harness, not product behavior; the scheduled Windows sweep is intended to execute tests, and this case only fails because the test id exposes the payload rather than using the existing short `label`. Attribution: introduced by commit 6724e79e8ff857b54dd36a62006a89445fc10ad6 (`rebar-ticket: 5931-78a3-95d2-44cd`), which added the long `("far_over_limit", "x" * 60_000)` parametrization without an explicit short id. Planned repair: make the parameter ids use the short labels so `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` remains below Windows’ env-var ceiling while leaving the real 60,000-character product input in the test body.
